idiom_name: assert statement (-ea) plus explicit invariant method
implementation_notes: The assert statement (JLS 14.10) is Java's assertion facility: disabled unless the class is started with -ea, throwing AssertionError when enabled. The Oracle guide's recipe is still the canonical realization - postconditions and class invariants inside the class via assert, while preconditions on public methods are enforced with explicit IllegalArgumentException or Objects.requireNonNull checks that work even when assertions are disabled; the same guide shows an aggregated invariant method (assert balanced()) called before each return. There is no built-in design-by-contract machinery, so require/ensure/invariant clauses must be hand-written or supplied by a tool such as JML.
pitfalls: Assertions are disabled by default: CI must run the JVM with -ea, and a forgotten flag silently converts every invariant check into dead code.
Because an assert may be compiled out, its expression must not change state; Oracle's assertion guidance also says not to use it for argument checking in public methods.
AssertionError extends Error and is meant never to be caught; a catch (Throwable) logging block swallows invariant violations.
An aggregated invariant() method costs O(size) on every call, so calling assert invariant() in a hot loop changes the profile even with assertions enabled.
